**Class** in the `Latiprimere.Cups` namespace, from the [Latiprimere.Cups](/docs/reference/#latiprimerecups) package.

```csharp
public sealed class CupsOptions
```

Configures how Latiprimere connects to CUPS.

## Constructors

```csharp
public CupsOptions()
```

## Properties

### ConnectTimeout

```csharp
public TimeSpan ConnectTimeout { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the longest wait for a TCP connection to the CUPS server to open. Defaults to [CupsOptions.DefaultConnectTimeout](/docs/reference/latiprimere-cups/cupsoptions/#defaultconnecttimeout), 10 seconds; without a limit, a server address with nothing behind it can take about 21 seconds to fail on Windows. Connections through the scheduler's Unix domain socket open at once or fail at once, so this doesn't apply to them.

It covers opening the connection only, not waiting for an answer. When it runs out, the request fails with a [PrintException](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printexception/).

**Exceptions**

- [ArgumentOutOfRangeException](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentoutofrangeexception): The value is not positive, or is longer than about 24 days.

### Credentials

```csharp
public NetworkCredential? Credentials { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the user name and password to authenticate with, or `null`, the default, to send none.

A standard CUPS installation needs no password to print, or to check or cancel your own jobs. Servers set up to ask for one answer with a [PrintAuthenticationException](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printauthenticationexception/) until it is set; catch that to ask the user, then create the print system again.

They are sent with every request, as HTTP Basic authentication, and over TCP they are encrypted by default: see [CupsOptions.Encryption](/docs/reference/latiprimere-cups/cupsoptions/#encryption). The [NetworkCredential.Domain](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.net.networkcredential.domain) is not used.

### Encryption

```csharp
public CupsEncryption Encryption { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets when TCP connections to the server are encrypted. Defaults to [CupsEncryption.Automatic](/docs/reference/latiprimere-cups/cupsencryption/#values): encrypted when [CupsOptions.Credentials](/docs/reference/latiprimere-cups/cupsoptions/#credentials) are set.

CUPS creates a self-signed certificate for itself unless given another, and .NET doesn't trust one of those. To connect to such a server, check its certificate in [CupsOptions.ServerCertificateValidationCallback](/docs/reference/latiprimere-cups/cupsoptions/#servercertificatevalidationcallback).

**Exceptions**

- [ArgumentOutOfRangeException](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentoutofrangeexception): The value is not one of the enumeration's values.

### Server

```csharp
public string? Server { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the CUPS server to use, in the same form as the `CUPS_SERVER` environment variable: either the path of the scheduler's Unix domain socket (for example `/run/cups/cups.sock`), or a host name with an optional port (for example `printserver:631`).

When `null`, Latiprimere uses `CUPS_SERVER` if set, then the local scheduler's socket, then `localhost:631`. Setting a server explicitly also allows CUPS to be used from Windows.

### ServerCertificateValidationCallback

```csharp
public RemoteCertificateValidationCallback? ServerCertificateValidationCallback { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the check of the server's certificate on encrypted connections, or `null`, the default, for the standard check against the trusted certificate authorities and the host name.

Use it to trust a server's self-signed certificate, by comparing the certificate with one you know is the server's, for example by its thumbprint. Accepting every certificate gives up the protection encryption is for: anyone able to intercept the connection could read the password.

### UserName

```csharp
public string? UserName { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the user name sent with requests as `requesting-user-name`, which CUPS uses to decide who owns a job. When `null`, the user name of [CupsOptions.Credentials](/docs/reference/latiprimere-cups/cupsoptions/#credentials) is used if set, otherwise the current operating-system user name.

It isn't a login: CUPS trusts this name without checking it. For a server that asks for a password, set [CupsOptions.Credentials](/docs/reference/latiprimere-cups/cupsoptions/#credentials); once a request is authenticated, CUPS uses the authenticated user instead.
